Customer interested in tighter cost controls and evaluating Redwood Dedicated vs hosted for PHI workloads. Agreed next steps: send cost workbook, schedule technical deep dive, share security pack.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-20
Time: 15:00 - 15:42 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Emma Li (Redwood AE), Maya Thompson (Redwood CSM), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Menon (Auriga Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Auriga CTO), Sara Ruiz (Auriga Platform Eng), Raj Patel (Auriga Product)

[00:00] Emma Li: hey everyone thanks for joining the QBR, uh appreciate you making time, we'll keep to about 40 minutes, agenda is usage and cost, reliability review, roadmap alignment and next steps. Maya and Daniel with me today.

[00:32] Liam O'Connor: yep thanks Emma, quick ask — can we also touch on data residency notes at the end? our legal team pinged about PHI flows.

[00:45] Maya Thompson: absolutely, we'll cover security at the end and i'll drop the pack after.

[01:10] Daniel Park: i'll be able to answer the infra sizing and latency questions, also i pulled sample traces from the last two weeks which we'll reference.

[02:15] Emma Li: ok first, usage highlights - Auriga's token consumption is up ~28% this quarter, mostly due to the triage assistant roll-out in May, average payload sizes increased. your cost per 1k tokens on hosted has been steady but overall bill increased. we flagged a couple of high-cost routes.

[03:00] Dr. Priya Menon: yes that's correct, triage assistant is in prod in three hospitals now; we expected usage to grow. we did see one spike when the patient intake flow retried multiple times, that blew up tokens.

[03:30] Emma Li: right, on the spike — Daniel, can you summarize what we saw?

[03:40] Daniel Park: sure, the trace shows a retry loop at about 2026-05-14 11:12 UTC, the frontend retried due to a 504 from a proxy, that multiplied token usage by ~6x for short window. not Redwood runtime issue directly; looked like our gateway timed out, but we had an open fallback to the larger context model which increased per-request token count.

[04:15] Sara Ruiz: just to call out, that gateway was an internal infra change we deployed to reduce latency, unfortunately we missed a retry header. we'll fix that.

[04:40] Emma Li: good, that helps. for cost controls we recommended prefix caching and route-level quotas, plus a batching profile change for triage assistant. Maya, you want to add?

[04:55] Maya Thompson: yeah, we also have an Optimize suggestion — a quantization profile for the triage model that would lower tokens/cost slightly when you can accept lower precision on summaries. i will attach the recommendation doc.

[05:30] Liam O'Connor: we're cautious about quantization for clinical summaries, accuracy matters. any data on quality regressions?

[05:45] Daniel Park: brief answer — for summarization it's usually safe at q4/8bit profiles for non-diagnostic text. we can run side-by-side evals on your prompt set. if you want we can do a canary on a small traffic percentage.

[06:20] Dr. Priya Menon: yes please run evals. priya: can we include the compression of long notes? that's where we see most tokens.

[06:40] Emma Li: noted. next section: reliability. we logged two incidents in Q2, one was the gateway retry incident and a second shorter outage in April where a Dedicated customer autoscaler triggered cross-tenant contention, actually that was on our side but i think we mitigated quickly.

[07:10] Raj Patel: do you have an RCA for the April outage? our compliance team saw an alert.

[07:20] Maya Thompson: yes, short version — kernel-level scheduling on a particular GPU host caused a temporary stall, it affected less than 0.5% of requests and we evicted the tenant, added a hotfix. i'll send the full RCA doc.

[07:40] Liam O'Connor: ok good to have that on record for auditors. also curious about SLOs — our internal SLO is 200ms P95 for short prompts, are we within that?

[08:05] Daniel Park: for your short prompt class P95 is currently 210ms on hosted. Most of the small variance is due to cold-path model loads and KV cache misses. for Dedicated pilot we can ensure instance pinning to keep you below 200ms.

[08:35] Emma Li: and Dedicated would also give more predictable throughput and isolation for PHI workloads per our earlier conversations.

[09:00] Dr. Priya Menon: timeline wise we are evaluating Dedicated for a pilot — what's the typical lead time?

[09:10] Emma Li: typical lead time is 3-6 weeks for initial capacity depending on GPU type and region, Daniel will size based on your QPS and seq lengths.

[09:35] Daniel Park: yes i'll need your 90th percentile sequence lengths and the expected concurrency per route. i pulled 30-day percentiles but we should refine for the triage flow.

[10:00] Sara Ruiz: we can export that this week, will share an S3 link.

[10:20] Emma Li: great. Roadmap alignment: we highlighted three upcoming features we think help you — 1) route-level soft quotas (rolling out July), 2) improved prefix caching (Aug beta), 3) VPC private control plane GA (Sept).

[10:50] Liam O'Connor: the VPC private control plane is critical for PHI — any compliance notes?

[11:05] Maya Thompson: it's designed for enterprise private deployments, includes KMS integration, full audit logs, and can be deployed into your VPC. we'll share the architecture diagram and SOC2/ISO artifacts.

[11:30] Dr. Priya Menon: that sounds promising. what's the pricing delta for private vs hosted?

[11:40] Emma Li: private has a platform fee plus committed monthly capacity; typically it's a step up from hosted as you get reserved GPUs and added controls. i'll send a model of estimated costs based on your current usage.

[12:05] Liam O'Connor: any quick wins for immediate cost reduction if we stay on hosted?

[12:15] Maya Thompson: yes — 1) apply route-level quotas and soft throttles, 2) enable prefix/KV caching for these triage flows, 3) evaluate low-cost model variants for non-clinical responses, 4) fix retry logic to avoid multiplicative spikes.

[13:00] Sara Ruiz: for caching, does Redwood support cross-request KV caching or just prefix?

[13:10] Daniel Park: both, though cross-request KV cache requires a compatible model and slightly different eviction policy; we'll recommend config.

[13:40] Emma Li: switching gears — security & compliance, Maya?

[13:50] Maya Thompson: we'll share the security pack: SOC2 report, ISO cert, data retention options, KMS/HSM integration notes, and the VPC private control plane spec. also note that audit logs can be retained per your retention policy.

[14:25] Liam O'Connor: do you support customer-managed keys in KMS for private?

[14:30] Maya Thompson: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported in Private and Dedicated environments.

[15:00] Dr. Priya Menon: excellent. question on logging — are token-level logs stored with PII redaction? we need to ensure no PHI is saved in plain text.

[15:20] Maya Thompson: logs are configurable; we can redact or hash sensitive fields. for PHI customers we recommend configuring redact rules and enabling the private control plane.

[16:00] Emma Li: okay quick recap of proposed next steps: Emma sends usage & cost workbook, Daniel schedules deep technical sizing and shares latency traces, Maya shares roadmap and security artifacts, customer to provide percentile exports and confirm pilot stakeholders.

[16:40] Liam O'Connor: timeline — we're aiming to decide on a Dedicated pilot by July 2, ideally kick-off mid July.

[17:00] Raj Patel: any blockers from your side on pilot capacity?

[17:08] Daniel Park: only that we finalize GPU type and region; otherwise we can reserve capacity once we have expected QPS.

[18:00] Dr. Priya Menon: can we run a short eval on quantized model for the non-diagnostic summarization? sounds like a low-risk test.

[18:15] Daniel Park: yes we can spin up a canary with q4/8bit and run A/B on your prompt-set for a week.

[18:40] Emma Li: i'll include that in the workbook as an option — run quantization eval during the pilot.

[19:00] [Long pause, cross talk about calendar invites and file links]

[20:30] Sara Ruiz: i'll upload the 90th/95th percentile seq lengths to the S3 link by EOD Friday.

[21:00] Emma Li: perfect. Daniel, can you confirm P95 target on Dedicated once sizing is done?

[21:10] Daniel Park: yes i'll provide expected P50/P95 numbers per config in the deep dive.

[21:30] Liam O'Connor: legal wants the PHI decision documented; any template you provide for the pilot contract?

[21:45] Maya Thompson: we have a pilot addendum template for PHI customers; i'll send that with the security pack.

[22:10] Dr. Priya Menon: one last thing — are there any upcoming price increases or billing model changes we should be aware of?

[22:25] Emma Li: none planned in the quarter; if anything changes we'll give 60 days notice and it's typically tied to new enterprise features.

[22:45] Raj Patel: good.

[23:00] [Wrap-up and confirmation of action items]

[23:10] Emma Li: thanks everyone, to summarize: we'll send the workbook and security docs, schedule technical deep-dive, run quantization eval during pilot, customer shares exports and confirms stakeholders. any other questions?

[23:30] Liam O'Connor: none from me, thanks.

[23:40] Dr. Priya Menon: thanks all.

[23:50] Emma Li: great, i'll follow up with the notes and links. bye.

[End of transcript — meeting length ~42 minutes]
